hens_rule_text: Up to 3 hens per residential parcel, with an annual poultry license from the City of Sacramento (Front Street Animal Shelter).
permit_notes: A poultry license/permit is required: about $30/year plus a $10 annual licensing fee per chicken, from the City of Sacramento Animal Care Front Street Animal Shelter.
setback_notes: Coop cannot be closer than 20 ft to the nearest neighboring dwelling.
coop_rules: Coop must be 15 to 42 sq ft, have four walls and a roof of suitable material, and be kept only in the rear yard; chickens must be confined in the coop at all times, and feces and feathers removed every 24 hours into airtight containers.
zoning_notes: Rules apply citywide under Sacramento City Code Sec. 9.44.860; Sacramento County, a separate jurisdiction, has its own different crowing-fowl and chicken rules that should not be confused with the city ordinance.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Sacramento City Code Sec. 9.44.860 (Keeping of chickens, unlawful, restrictions), amended by Ordinance No. 2011-039
